content.text:
I made two small fixes to `0.html`; neither has been tested in a browser, because the shell command I used to look for one was blocked in this session.

The file was already in good shape, so I limited the changes to things I could justify from reading the code:

1. **Rapid clicks were being swallowed** (`0.html:435`). Every click after the first in a fast run was ignored, so clicking quickly three or four times left you stuck on blue after the double-click reset. Now only the second click of a run is treated as the double-click; the third and later clicks cycle again. I also added a guard so the reset can't fire again on later even-numbered clicks in a run.

2. **Circle sizing on mobile** (`0.html:89`). The circle was sized against `60vh`, while the body already uses `100dvh`. I added a `60dvh` declaration, with the `vh` line kept as fallback, so the circle doesn't get sized against the taller viewport when mobile browser toolbars are showing.

The first fix changes behaviour: a fast second click still resets to blue, but further clicks now advance the colour instead of doing nothing. If the old swallowing was deliberate, revert the `event.detail === 2` check to `event.detail > 1`.

## Things I noticed but left alone

- **Double-click flicker:** a double-click first advances the colour, then resets it, so there is a brief flash and an extra screen-reader announcement. Fixing it means delaying every single click, which I judged worse.
- **Hint toggle shifts the layout:** toggling the `?` hint re-wraps the text and nudges the vertically centred circle.
- **No-JS hint:** without JavaScript the "Click to cycle" hint still shows alongside the noscript message.
